tools.title: lox/agent-harness
tools.summary: Minimal composable Go library that implements the core tool-calling agent loop with hooks and thread state.
tools.usecase: Use it to embed a tiny provider-agnostic agent loop inside Go services without pulling a full framework.

tools.title: OpenAgentHarness
tools.summary: Headless workspace-first agent engine exposing HTTP APIs for sessions, runs, actions, sandboxes and SSE streaming for embedded products.
tools.usecase: Use it as the backend runtime under your own chat UI and tenant model for internal agent platforms.

tools.title: OpenHarness (HKUDS)
tools.summary: Lightweight open agent infrastructure with tool loop, 43+ tools, skills, memory, multi-agent coordination, permissions and a personal ohmo gateway.
tools.usecase: Use it to run a self-hosted personal coding agent over chat channels that forks branches and opens PRs.

tools.title: RepoMaster
tools.summary: Repo-scoped research harness that builds function and module graphs so agents explore only needed context with lower token use on coding benches.

tools.title: SWE-bench
tools.summary: Canonical software-engineering benchmark and harness for issue-to-patch agent evaluation across real GitHub repositories.
tools.usecase: Use it to measure pass@1 of your coding harness on verified GitHub issues with official Docker runners.

tools.title: SWE-ReX
tools.summary: Sandboxed remote execution layer for AI agents that keeps the same API across local shells, Docker, Modal, Fargate and parallel sessions.
tools.usecase: Use it to run hundreds of coding-agent trajectories in parallel without rewriting agent logic for each backend.

tools.title: Terminal-Bench
tools.summary: Benchmark measuring agents on complicated real terminal workflows with Harbor as the official runner.
tools.usecase: Use it to score shell-native coding agents on multi-step terminal tasks with concurrent Harbor jobs.

tools.title: VoltAgent
tools.summary: Open-source TypeScript agent engineering platform with core runtime, workflows, supervisors, MCP tools, memory adapters, guardrails, and a paired observability console.
tools.usecase: Use it to spin up typed multi-agent teams with durable memory and production evals from a single create-voltagent-app scaffold.

tools.title: agent-harness
tools.summary: Provider-agnostic modular Python agent harness with Protocols for models, tools, sessions, and sandboxes plus async typed core under 3k LOC.
tools.usecase: Use it to assemble a custom loop that plugs Anthropic, OpenAI, Modal sandboxes, or Redis sessions without god-classes.

tools.title: Agentic Harness
tools.summary: Self-hosted completion gate that wraps coding agents with independent verification, durable evidence, CLI, and local GUI before reporting done.
tools.usecase: Use it to force an external check and report.md before any agent can claim a goal is finished across compatible CLIs.

tools.title: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)
tools.summary: Observability-driven system that automatically evolves coding-agent harness components such as prompts, tools, middleware, and memory while holding the base model fixed.
tools.usecase: Use it to iterate harness configs over evaluate-analyze-improve loops and freeze transferable components that lift Terminal-Bench scores.

tools.title: agentic-sandbox
tools.summary: Self-hostable runtime for persistent autonomous coding agents using KVM-isolated VMs or rootless containers with A2A protocol, dashboard, and virtiofs storage.
tools.usecase: Use it to run long-lived agent sessions on your own hardware with signed AgentCard discovery and mission dispatch without a hosted control plane.

tools.title: AgentTier
tools.summary: Kubernetes-native sandbox platform providing isolated persistent environments for AI agents and developers via CRDs with gVisor options and interactive access.
tools.usecase: Use it to provision secure sandboxes for coding agents or teams with declarative lifecycle, network isolation, and multi-agent orchestration.

tools.title: Blaxel Sandbox
tools.summary: Open-source microVM sandbox templates and hub for persistent agent compute with standby resume, MCP tools, filesystem, and process APIs.
tools.usecase: Use it to give agents dedicated Linux environments that resume in tens of milliseconds while keeping full state across idle periods.

tools.title: Codewhale
tools.summary: Open-source Rust terminal coding agent with multi-model support, fleets, MCP, hooks, approval modes, snapshots, and local-first extensibility.
tools.usecase: Use it to coordinate agent teams on repo tasks with explicit plan or full-access modes and undoable workspace restores.

tools.title: Codey
tools.summary: Multi-agent workbench that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi from a native macOS app, chat platforms, or voice with per-project workspaces.
tools.usecase: Use it to run parallel agents on the same prompt for comparison or define worker teams with flow graphs and messaging channels.

tools.title: HAR
tools.summary: Open agent harness CLI plus MCP that runs coding agents in isolated worktrees with deterministic launch, verify, and teardown stages.
tools.usecase: Use it to turn any repo into verified software-factory slots that wrap Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex with project-native checks.

tools.title: Harness
tools.summary: Rust control plane for fleets of parallel coding agents with orchestration, policy enforcement, cross-agent review, and observability.
tools.usecase: Use it to assign work, police permissions, and run independent reviews across Claude Code or Codex adapters in long-running fleets.

tools.title: jcode
tools.summary: High-performance Rust coding agent harness optimized for low RAM, fast boot, semantic memory graphs, side panels, and native swarm collaboration across sessions.
tools.usecase: Use it to run dozens of parallel coding sessions on limited hardware with automatic conflict notification and memory recall.

tools.title: OpenHarness
tools.summary: Local-first Python control plane for coding agents featuring Default, Plan, externally judged Goals, sandboxed execution, durable context, plugins, and evals.
tools.usecase: Use it to drive REPL sessions with independent judges that decide continue, complete, or pause based on artifacts rather than agent claims.

tools.title: openteams
tools.summary: Local-first AI desktop app that plans, builds, and ships with a controllable team of coding agents including many popular CLIs plus a bundled CLI.
tools.usecase: Use it to assign roles across Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and others inside one workspace with budget caps and reviewer loops.

tools.title: Pi
tools.summary: Minimal extensible coding agent harness with unified multi-provider LLM API, agent core loop, TUI, skills, extensions, and session persistence.
tools.usecase: Use it to build or extend a lean coding CLI that stays small at core while adding TypeScript packages for custom tools and themes.

tools.title: remote-swe-agents
tools.summary: Self-hosted fully open-source autonomous SWE agent example on AWS that works in dedicated cloud environments and opens PRs.
tools.usecase: Use it to run laptop-free coding agents that clone, edit, test, and submit pull requests inside isolated AWS workspaces.

tools.title: Sandboxer
tools.summary: Unified client libraries in Go, Python, and TypeScript that talk directly to E2B, Daytona, Blaxel, Runloop, Fly, or local Docker sandboxes.
tools.usecase: Use it to switch sandbox providers behind one mental model for create, exec, filesystem, and teardown without rewriting agent code.

tools.title: SWE Forge
tools.summary: Portable opt-in workflow orchestration that sits above coding harnesses to turn tickets into bounded inspect-plan-implement-verify-review deliveries.
tools.usecase: Use it to add evidence-backed SOLO or SUBAGENTS topologies over Pi, OpenCode, or experimental Claude Code adapters without replacing the base harness.

tools.title: SWE-AF
tools.summary: Autonomous software engineering fleet runtime that spins up planners, coders, reviewers, and testers to ship production-grade PRs from a single goal call.
tools.usecase: Use it to orchestrate multi-repo builds with dependency scheduling, git worktrees, and adaptive factory control for end-to-end delivery.

tools.title: SWE-agent
tools.summary: LM-driven harness built for SWE-bench that provides edit state, command execution, and an issue-focused loop as a reference agent-computer interface.
tools.usecase: Use it to clone a battle-tested issue-to-PR agent stack and adapt the YAML config for custom benchmarks or cybersecurity tasks.

tools.title: TrueForge
tools.summary: Open-source agent harness runtime that handles model calls, MCP tools, skills, sandboxing, approvals, context compaction, and session state with chat UI plus TypeScript SDK.
tools.usecase: Use it to deploy cost-controlled multi-step agents locally or hosted while swapping any model provider and MCP servers.

tools.title: Agent Sandbox
tools.summary: Kubernetes CRD and controller for isolated, stateful, singleton workloads tailored to AI agent runtimes and RL, with warm pools and stable identity.
tools.usecase: Use it to declare and manage long-lived agent sandboxes on any K8s cluster with pause/resume and template claims.

tools.title: Agent Security Harness
tools.summary: Adversarial testing harness with hundreds of executable protocol-level tests for MCP, A2A, and governance controls.
tools.usecase: Use it to CI-gate agent endpoints by actively probing for policy bypass and tool poisoning.

tools.title: Agenta
tools.summary: Open-source workspace for building, versioning, and collaborating on agents and automations with MCP and self-hosting.
tools.usecase: Use it to prototype and share agent workflows as a team with prompt and skill management.

tools.title: AgentTeams
tools.summary: Collaborative multi-agent OS using Matrix rooms for transparent human-in-the-loop coordination across heterogeneous runtimes.
tools.usecase: Use it to run mixed OpenClaw, Hermes, and other workers in shared rooms with file exchange and audit.

tools.title: AIO Sandbox
tools.summary: Single Docker container packing browser, shell, filesystem, MCP servers, VSCode Server, and Jupyter for unified agent environments.
tools.usecase: Use it to give coding or computer-use agents one shared sandbox with VNC, CDP, and MCP endpoints.

tools.title: Chorus
tools.summary: CLI harness pattern for multi-LLM peer review before shipping code, listed among rising terminal agent tooling.
tools.usecase: Use it to add a multi-model review gate in front of any coding agent commit flow.

tools.title: Coze Loop
tools.summary: Full-lifecycle agent optimization platform covering development, debugging, evaluation, and monitoring.
tools.usecase: Use it to instrument and iterate on agent workflows with playgrounds, evals, and production monitoring.

tools.title: Crush
tools.summary: Go-native terminal coding agent with polished TUI, LSP intelligence, multi-provider switching mid-session, MCP extensibility, and session persistence.
tools.usecase: Use it to run provider-agnostic agentic coding sessions directly in the terminal with LSP-backed edits and MCP tools.

tools.title: CubeSandbox
tools.summary: RustVMM/KVM microVM sandbox service with sub-60ms boot, hardware isolation, under 5MB overhead, and E2B SDK drop-in compatibility.
tools.usecase: Use it to self-host high-density, hardware-isolated code execution backends for agent tool calls.

tools.title: Headroom
tools.summary: Content-aware compression layer for tool outputs, logs, and RAG chunks that claims large token reductions for coding agents.
tools.usecase: Use it to shrink context before it hits the model while preserving answer quality on long agent runs.

tools.title: Kimi Code CLI
tools.summary: Single-binary terminal coding agent with fast TUI startup, skills, MCP, and ACP IDE integration, model-agnostic beyond Kimi defaults.
tools.usecase: Use it to install a zero-Node coding agent that reads, edits, shells, and plans inside any repo.

tools.title: LiteLLM
tools.summary: Unified interface and proxy for 100-plus LLMs with routing, caching, budgets, and agent SDK gateways.
tools.usecase: Use it as the model router and spend control plane in front of any custom harness.

tools.title: metaharness
tools.summary: Scaffold that generates a focused, branded agent harness with npx CLI, MCP server, scoped memory, skills, and witness-signed releases for multiple host runtimes.
tools.usecase: Use it to spin up a repo-specific harness that drops into existing coding agents with governance and provenance.

tools.title: Mission Control
tools.summary: Self-hosted control plane for dispatching tasks, reviewing runs, tracking spend, and operating multiple agent runtimes.
tools.usecase: Use it to operate fleets of coding agents with observability, spend controls, and task queues.

tools.title: NanoClaw
tools.summary: Lightweight container-isolated AI assistant inspired by larger claw-style agents, designed for readable code and secure defaults.
tools.usecase: Use it to deploy per-agent containers with shared rooms while keeping the codebase small enough to audit.

tools.title: Qwen Code
tools.summary: Open-source terminal coding agent with auto-memory, skills, sub-agents, teams, MCP, plan mode, and multi-protocol support optimized for Qwen coder models.
tools.usecase: Use it to run headless or interactive agentic coding workflows with free OAuth tiers and IDE plugins.

tools.title: Roo Code
tools.summary: VS Code and Cursor extension in the Cline lineage with approval-gated modes, strong MCP support, and custom agent modes.
tools.usecase: Use it for plan-then-act coding inside the editor with per-step gates and MCP tools.

tools.title: Strands Agents
tools.summary: Open-source Python and TypeScript SDK for building production agent loops with lifecycle controls, MCP, memory, multi-agent patterns, guardrails, and evals.
tools.usecase: Use it to replace hand-rolled agent loops with a portable, model-agnostic harness you control end-to-end.

tools.title: Trae Agent
tools.summary: Research-friendly Python CLI agent for software engineering with modular architecture and multi-LLM support.
tools.usecase: Use it to prototype SWE-bench style loops or modular coding agents without heavy product shells.

tools.title: ZeroClaw
tools.summary: Single Rust binary agent runtime with multi-channel support, provider plugins, supervised autonomy, and OS-level sandbox options.
tools.usecase: Use it to run a low-overhead personal or team agent across Discord, Telegram, and CLI with policy gates.

tools.title: agent-harness
tools.summary: Plan-native execution harness adding intent-to-contract synthesis, durable handoff, and evidence-based acceptance.
tools.usecase: Use it to add portable contracts and audit gates across Codex, Claude Code, or other file-and-shell agents.

tools.title: agentOS
tools.summary: Lightweight WASM and V8 isolate OS library that runs agents inside your process with millisecond cold starts and direct host bindings.
tools.usecase: Use it to embed Pi or other ACP agents as in-process VMs with granular permissions instead of spinning full sandboxes.

tools.title: Agno
tools.summary: Framework and AgentOS runtime for building, serving, and managing agent platforms with UI control plane.
tools.usecase: Use it to own your full agent stack including sessions, memory, traces, and MCP in your own cloud.

tools.title: AIOS
tools.summary: AI Agent Operating System with kernel and SDK for scheduling, context, memory, tools, and computer-use sandboxes.
tools.usecase: Use it to treat agents as first-class OS processes with shared resource management and deployment modes.

tools.title: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.summary: Official MCP server exposing full Chrome DevTools for automation, performance traces, network, console, and debugging.
tools.usecase: Use it to let an agent inspect LCP, take heap snapshots, or drive live Chrome sessions during coding tasks.

tools.title: Composio
tools.summary: Tool layer with 1000+ integrations, auth, search, and sandboxed workbench so agents stop reinventing OAuth.
tools.usecase: Use it to drop authenticated toolkits into any agent harness for Gmail, GitHub, Slack, and more.

tools.title: Deep Agents
tools.summary: Batteries-included opinionated agent harness on LangGraph with planning, filesystem tools, sub-agents, and context management.
tools.usecase: Use it to spin up a production-ready long-horizon research or coding agent and override only the pieces you need.

tools.title: dmux
tools.summary: Dev agent multiplexer that creates git worktrees and tmux panes for parallel coding agents.
tools.usecase: Use it to launch isolated agent sessions per task then merge or PR the results from a single board.

tools.title: E2B Desktop
tools.summary: Open-source virtual desktop sandbox for computer-use agents with graphical environment and streaming.
tools.usecase: Use it to give agents a full isolated desktop for GUI automation and secure code execution.

tools.title: Graphiti
tools.summary: Framework for building temporal knowledge graphs that track changing facts with provenance for agent memory.
tools.usecase: Use it to give agents a real-time context graph that invalidates stale facts and supports hybrid retrieval.

tools.title: Harness Kit
tools.summary: Multi-agent orchestration CLI plus task board with TDD-first patterns, RCA, and cost-aware delegation.
tools.usecase: Use it to decompose specs into dependency graphs, route tasks to cheapest capable agents, and keep evidence trails.

tools.title: Kit
tools.summary: Coding agent runtime with one compose tool, ACP server, A2A, and subagent orchestration in a static binary.
tools.usecase: Use it as a concise daily-driver harness that reloads skills and MCP dynamically and hosts other agents over ACP.

tools.title: Letta Code
tools.summary: Memory-first stateful coding agent that persists identity and long-term memory across sessions and models.
tools.usecase: Use it to run coding agents that learn from experience and retain context without prompt stuffing.

tools.title: mcp-use
tools.summary: TypeScript framework for building MCP servers and apps rebuilt for the stateless 2026 MCP spec.
tools.usecase: Use it to ship high-throughput MCP servers with inspector, HMR views, and headless screenshot debugging for agents.

tools.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.summary: Lightweight provider-agnostic framework for multi-agent workflows with handoffs, guardrails, and tracing.
tools.usecase: Use it to compose specialist agents with structured handoffs and run them against any tool-calling LLM.

tools.title: PraisonAI
tools.summary: Fast multi-agent workforce framework with planning, memory, RAG, dashboards, and multi-provider support.
tools.usecase: Use it to spin up autonomous agent teams with low-latency orchestration for production workflows.

tools.title: Pydantic AI
tools.summary: Typed Python AI SDK and agent framework with structured outputs, multi-model support, and MCP integration.
tools.usecase: Use it to build type-safe agent loops with validated I/O and Logfire observability for production services.

tools.title: smolagents
tools.summary: Barebones Python library for code-as-action agents that write and execute Python in sandboxes like E2B.
tools.usecase: Use it to prototype multi-step agents that compose tools via real code rather than JSON tool calls.

tools.title: Stagehand
tools.summary: SDK for browser agents built on Playwright with natural language actions, self-healing, and multi-language support.
tools.usecase: Use it to give coding or research agents reliable web navigation and extraction without brittle selectors.

tools.title: VT Code
tools.summary: Rust terminal coding agent and harness with sandboxed tools, durable sessions, MCP, skills, and multi-provider support.
tools.usecase: Use it to run long autonomous coding loops from a TUI or headless mode with built-in verification and worktree isolation.

tools.title: Agenvoy
tools.summary: Self-hosted AI agent harness in a single Go binary. Writes, sandbox-tests, and repairs its own code. No Electron, no account.
tools.usecase: Use it as a local coding worker you can scp onto a box and run unattended against a failing test suite.

tools.title: cmux
tools.summary: Open-source Ghostty-based macOS terminal with vertical tabs and notifications for AI coding agents.
tools.usecase: Use it as the terminal surface when you are running a swarm of CLIs and need to see which one just finished.

tools.title: Containarium
tools.summary: Open-source agent runtime with SSH-native isolation, eBPF egress policy, Kubernetes and LXC backends.
tools.usecase: Use it to run untrusted coding agents with real network policy instead of hope.

tools.title: context-mode
tools.summary: Context-window surgery for coding agents. Sandboxes tool output so the model sees the signal instead of a 40k-token log.
tools.usecase: Use it when your agent keeps blowing the window on build logs and you need the loop to survive a real compile.

tools.title: CUA
tools.summary: Open-source computer-use 2.0: drivers, cross-OS fleets, and benchmarks for training and evaluating desktop agents.
tools.usecase: Use it to give a coding agent a real desktop when the job is a GUI installer, not an API.

tools.title: DeepCode
tools.summary: Open agentic coding from HKU: agent harness, loop engineering, multi-agent orchestration. Academic lab software that ships as a repo you run.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want a research harness with a real coding loop, not a chatbot with extra steps.

tools.title: Ghostex
tools.summary: Rust and GPUI native agent CLI manager for macOS. Ghostty terminals plus Codex-app UX, without Electron.
tools.usecase: Use it to manage a stack of native agent CLIs in Ghostty instead of a webview IDE.

tools.title: graff
tools.summary: Fast agentic coding harness in Zig: multi-provider, MCP, workflows.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want a coding loop with systems-language latency, not a Node daemon.

tools.title: Herdr
tools.summary: The runtime your coding agents live on. Not another chat wrapper: a place agents persist, resume, and share a machine.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want agents to survive a laptop sleep and pick up the same checkout, secrets, and tools.

tools.title: Ironcurtain
tools.summary: Secure runtime for autonomous agents. Policy from plain-English constitutions.
tools.usecase: Use it when you will not give a coding agent root and still want it to act.

tools.title: LoopX
tools.summary: A long-horizon control plane that keeps coding agents on durable, governed work instead of one-shot chats. Power users treat it as the supervisor, not another model.
tools.usecase: Use it to keep an overnight refactor alive across tool crashes, with a human gate on the risky steps.

tools.title: mcp-agent
tools.summary: Build effective agents with Model Context Protocol and small workflow patterns.
tools.usecase: Use it to compose MCP servers into a durable agent without standing up a full IDE plugin.

tools.title: mini-SWE-agent
tools.summary: The 100-line AI agent from the Princeton SWE-agent line. Research origin, radical simplicity, still beating bloated wrappers on SWE-bench-class work.
tools.usecase: Use it to throw a GitHub issue at a 100-line loop you can actually read, fork, and instrument.

tools.title: Mnemon
tools.summary: LLM-supervised persistent memory for agents: graph recall, cross-session knowledge, no vector-store cargo cult.
tools.usecase: Use it to give a coding agent a graph of the last two weeks of decisions so it stops re-deriving your architecture.

tools.title: oh-my-agent
tools.summary: A multi-agent harness that checks the work by artifacts, not vibes. Stop-hooks verify diffs, tests, and files before the run is allowed to claim success.
tools.usecase: Use it to stop a coding agent from declaring done when the test file was never written.

tools.title: oh-my-claudecode
tools.summary: Teams-first multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code. Not Claude Code itself: the swarm layer people bolt on.
tools.usecase: Use it to run a team of Claude Code workers on one repo with a shared plan file.

tools.title: oh-my-pi
tools.summary: A coding agent with the IDE wired in. Created New Year's Eve 2025, still being pushed daily.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want the agent and the editor to share one process instead of a plugin talking to a CLI.

tools.title: Omnigent
tools.summary: Open-source meta-harness: one orchestrator that fans work across several coding agents. Born June 2026, already the loudest new control plane on GitHub.
tools.usecase: Use it to run three different coding agents on the same ticket and merge the first one that lands a green test.

tools.title: open-computer-use
tools.summary: Computer-use agents on open models plus an E2B desktop sandbox. The open alternative to a vendor's computer-use API.
tools.usecase: Use it to let an open model click through a desktop app inside a throwaway VM.

tools.title: Orca
tools.summary: An ADE for a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent against your repo in parallel panes instead of one blessed CLI.
tools.usecase: Use it to fan the same failing test across four agents and keep only the patch that compiles.

tools.title: OSWorld 2.0
tools.summary: Long-horizon computer-use benchmark. The eval serious desktop-agent repos cite.
tools.usecase: Use it to grade your own computer-use agent on real desktop tasks before you trust it on a laptop.

tools.title: Warren
tools.summary: Treats coding agents as infrastructure, not terminal sessions. Isolation, lifetimes, and scheduling so a fleet of agents looks like a job queue.
tools.usecase: Use it to fire 20 isolated agent jobs against a monorepo without them trampling each other's working trees.

tools.title: Whip
tools.summary: Fast coding-agent harness in Go. Tool-use loop, bubbletea TUI, provider-routable models. Created August 2026.
tools.usecase: Use it as a Go TUI coding agent when you want to swap models without swapping the loop.

tools.title: CLI Agent Orchestrator
